units.la: Ille enim dies ab initio mundi fuit sanctificatus à Deo, & suo cultui destinatus, ut facile intelligitur Gen. 2. 3, Exo. 20. 11. Ergo is fuit solemnis Ecclesiastici conuentus dies. Disciplina ecclesiastica hac fuit, Quod Excommunicationis vsum Deus ipse in Ecclesia instituerat, dum Cainum eiecit à facie sua, & eum censura pœnaque ista primus ferit. Quod genus Ecclesiasticæ pœnæ postea, Ecclesiaq; vsurpatum, ut infrà ostendetur. Vtrũ autem ea tota ætate fuerit Idololatria, id est, homines præsertim Caini posteri idola pro vero Deo coluerint, velut Cainum ipsum generis sui autorem, quem Graeci Zῆνα, Latini Iouem postea dixerunt, dubium est. Putat enim Philo Iudæus Idola tunc à Tubalcaino fuisse fabricata & culta. Et Epiphanius Idololatriam demum temporibus Thara patris Abrahami introduxit, notamque fuisse inter Mortales exitiosam. Sed hæc haetenus.
units.tr: For that day had been sanctified by God from the beginning of the world and set apart for his worship, as is readily understood from Gen. 2:3 and Exod. 20:11. Therefore it was the solemn day of ecclesiastical assembly. Church discipline was this: God himself had instituted the use of excommunication in the Church when he cast Cain out from his face, and he was the first to strike him with this censure and punishment. This kind of ecclesiastical penalty was afterwards taken up and used by the Church, as will be shown below. Whether there was idolatry throughout that whole age, that is, whether men, especially the posterity of Cain, worshipped idols in place of the true God, worshipping Cain himself as the author of their race, whom the Greeks later called Zen [Ζῆνα] and the Latins Jupiter, is doubtful. For Philo the Jew thinks that idols were then made and worshipped by Tubalcain. And Epiphanius places the introduction of idolatry only in the times of Terah, father of Abraham, and says that it was known among mortals as a pernicious thing. But so much for these matters.

units.la: LIBER SEV SECTIO TERTIA PRIMAE MVNDI AETATIS, QVAE CONTINET PVBLICAM Nominis Dei Profanationem, & quae postea vsque ad Annum vniuersalis Diluuij contigerunt. Habet autem annos à Creatione Mundi, 1655. A Profanatione Nominis Dei, 1421. CAPVT I.
units.tr: LIBER SEV SECTIO TERTIA PRIMAE MVNDI AETATIS: BOOK OR SECTION THREE OF THE FIRST AGE OF THE WORLD, WHICH CONTAINS THE PUBLIC PROFANATION OF THE NAME OF GOD, AND WHAT HAPPENED AFTERWARDS UNTIL THE YEAR OF THE UNIVERSAL FLOOD. It covers 1655 years from the Creation of the World, and 1421 from the Profanation of the Name of God. CHAPTER I.

units.la: Continet Historica XII.
units.tr: This contains twelve historical chapters.

units.la: VTRA quidem complexi sumus & extendimus secundum seculum Prime Aetatis huius Mundi, vsq; ad publicam Nominis Diuini Profanationem, que incidit, vt diximus, (atque etiam ex S. Historia facile colligitur) in annum à Mundo condito 235. Quod tempus natiuitas Sethi (qui fuit filius Adami) precurrit. Natus enim est anno à condito mundo 130. detractis duntaxat diebus septem, post quos à Deo creatus est Adamus. Ergo frustra iam repeti vi-S. deretur illa natiuitas Sethi, quoniam inter illam, & immanem publicumque Nominis Dei contemptum (qui centum & quinque totis annis postea contigit, si modo concesserimus Mosem ordinem seriemq; temporis esse secutum, quod maximè verum indico) quoniam, inquâ, intra illam Sethi procreationem ex Adamo, & publicam istam Nominis, maiestatisque Diuina totius irrisionem, & abiectionem S. Scriptura nullam notabilem ἐποχὴν notat vel obseruat, neque nouum rarumq; euentu quicquam euenit. Ergo & nos quoque antea totius istius prima Mundi aetatis facilius distinguëda, & memoria commendanda gratiâ, natiuitatem Sethi sub priore proximéque precedenti seculo comprehendimus, quâ neque nunc repetimus, quoniam supra à nobis explicata est abunde: sed ab eo, quod coniunctum est cum ista profanatione nominis Dei, ordiemur. Est autem Natiuitas Enoschi seu Enochi ex Setho, à qua ad tempus ipsum vniuersalis Diluuij tertiam sectionem seu partem seu seculum tertium prima Mundi aetatis extendimus, & complectimur. Habet autem hoc temporis spatium à Creatione Mundi annos 1656. Ab ipsa Profanatione Nominis Dei, annos 1421. Praecessit enim tanto temporis & annorum numero Diluuium hac Profanatio. Continet historica capita duodecim, è quibus est
units.tr: Indeed, we have both comprehended and extended the second century of this First Age of the World down to the public profanation of God's Name, which, as we have said (and as is easily gathered from Sacred History as well), fell in the year 235 from the creation of the world. That period is preceded by the birth of Seth, who was the son of Adam. For he was born in the year 130 from the founding of the world, minus only seven days, after which Adam was created by God. So it would be pointless to repeat here that birth of Seth, since between the begetting of Seth from Adam and that public and monstrous contempt and rejection of the Name and majesty of God (which occurred a hundred and five full years later, if we grant that Moses followed the order and sequence of time, which I think most true), Sacred Scripture marks or notes no notable epoch [ἐποχὴν] between Seth's begetting from Adam and that public mockery and abjection of the whole divine majesty, and nothing new or rare happened. Therefore, so that this whole first age of the world may be more easily divided and committed to memory, we have included the birth of Seth under the earlier and immediately preceding century, which we do not repeat now, since it has been sufficiently explained above by us. Instead we shall begin with what is joined to this profanation of God's Name. The birth of Enosch, or Enoch, from Seth is where we begin, and from it down to the very time of the universal Flood we extend and embrace the third section, or part, or third century of the First Age of the World. This span of time covers 1656 years from the Creation of the World, and 1421 from the Profanation of the Name of God itself, for this profanation preceded the Flood by so many years. It contains twelve historical chapters, of which the first is

units.la: I. Natiuitas Enochi, seu, quemadmodum alij scribunt, & verius, Enoschi.
units.tr: I. The birth of Enoch, or, as others write, and more correctly, Enosch.

units.la: ABELE occisô, videbatur spes propagandæ in Mundo Ecclesiæ (postquam extinctus foret Adamus) prorsus sublata. Nam solus Cainus eiusq; posteri viri,licet industry,tamen impij restabant ac assfundebantur, qui & Dei contemptum inducebant in Mundum, & omne vitij nefarij genus. Adamus quidem ipse,& Eua Deũ timebant:sed quoniam erant mortales, prorsus tandem Dei cultus, & Ecclesia post eos sublatos videbatur peritura. Cui malo & desperationi Deus vt mederetur, Adamo Sethum dedit filium, quem illi Abelis pij loco substituit Gen.4.25: ac propterea eum Sethum Adamum nominauit,tanquâ sibi repositũ à Deo,restitutúmque semen,pium nempe virum eum futurum_, & Dei timentem præsagiens. Natus verò tunc erat Adamus annos 130. quum Sethum ex Eua suscepit, Gen. 5.3. Ergo in Setho denuo instaurata fuit Ecclesia,vel potius prima eius Propagatio condita,præparata,fundataq̃. Nam ex Setho postea natus est Enoschus vir Dei & pius,vti & ex Enoscho alij,quos recenset Moses. Erat autem annorum 105 Sethus, antequâ Enoschum procrearet,vllúmque successorem,heredem & spem continuanda pietatis & Ecclesia, promissionisque illius Dei de futuro Messia seruanda Mundum haberet: adeo vt totis 235 annis ante hunc Enoschum Sethi filium, Adami nepotem,Dei cultus propagatorem, impietas,iniustitiáque in Mundo fuerit liberè grassata, & per liberos Caini iam plures,atq; per varias familias & terras iam quoque multiplicatos auĉla,confirmata,& cõstabilita,adeo vt publica nominis Dei Profanatio tandem obtinuerit inter mortales,inualuerit̃q; Gen 4 26. Ergo in Sethi familia & edibus adhuc velut puella adolescebat Ecclesia Dei, quũ iam in Caini posteris esset. adulta robustáque fraus, improbitas hominum, malitia, Deo contemptio, si modo fateamur Mosem in historia sua contexenda rationem seriémque temporis secutum esse, quod verum est. Quare Boni & pii viri, ex Setho: Mali & impii ex Caino nati sunt, ac propagantur.
units.tr: With Abel slain, the hope of propagating the Church in the world seemed utterly lost (after Adam himself had died). For only Cain and his posterity remained, men who were industrious but wicked, and they multiplied and spread both contempt of God and every kind of nefarious vice through the world. Adam himself and Eve feared God, but since they were mortal, it seemed that the worship of God and the Church would perish once they were gone. To remedy this evil and despair, God gave Adam a son, Seth, whom He put in the place of the pious Abel (Gen. 4:25). Adam therefore named him Seth, as one restored to him by God, a seed given back, foreseeing that he would be a pious man who feared God. Adam was then 130 years old when he begot Seth from Eve (Gen. 5:3). So the Church was renewed in Seth, or rather its first propagation was established, prepared and founded. For from Seth was afterwards born Enosch, a man of God and pious, and from Enosch others, whom Moses lists. Seth was 105 years old before he begot Enosch, and so before he had any successor, heir and hope for continuing piety and the Church, and for preserving that promise of God concerning the future Messiah. So for the whole 235 years before this Enosch, son of Seth, grandson of Adam and propagator of the worship of God, impiety and injustice ran freely in the world. Through the children of Cain, now multiplied into many families and lands, they grew, were confirmed and were established, until the public profanation of God's name at last prevailed among mortals and gained strength (Gen. 4:26). Therefore, in the household of Seth, the Church of God was still growing up like a young girl, while among the posterity of Cain it was already grown. Deceit, the wickedness of men, malice and contempt of God had grown adult and strong, if indeed we grant that Moses, in writing his history, followed the order and sequence of time, which is true. Therefore good and pious men were born and propagated from Seth, and evil and impious men from Cain.

units.la: II. Publica Nominis Dei Profanatio.
units.tr: II. The public profanation of the name of God.

units.la: PROPAGATO igitur peruersò illo Cainis genere, nullóque adhuc magno existente piorum numero, & stirpe sancta nondum multiplicata in Orbe, prolata, nec in ramos diffusa, sequebatur vt magna vitiorum vis & corroboratio esset, magnáque contrà virtutum inter mortales labefactatio, ac tandem earum interitus sequeretur. Et primùm quidem in Deum ipsum Homines Caini posteri iniuriy esse coeperunt, quem oculis non cernebant: Postea verò in proximos inter quos etiam versabantur, quosque oculis suis cernebant. Facilius enim impii in Deum sibi inconspicuum (quémque putant procul à se remotum) blasphemant, eumque contemnunt: quàm proximos suos laedat, quos vident, & cernunt esse sese tueri paratos, & sibi viribus pares, & quos propter communem inter se naturam ac societatem facilius diligunt, 1. Ioan. 4. 20, Gal. 5. 15. Atque hic Dei contemptus primùm ex immani hominum ambitione natus est, qui quùm se viderent industrios & robustos, rebusque tum necessarys ad hanc vitam, tum voluptarijs abundarent: & post artes repertas, quum eorum bonorum omnium laudem sibi suóque ingenio sacrilegè, non autem Deo vero illorum autori homines isti tribuerent, facilè eò sponte vltróque ipsi deuenerunt, & prolapsi sunt, vt Deum ipsum negligerent: se autem ipsos admirarētur, & solos spectarent. Ergo Dei contemptus paulatim inter eiusmodi mortales nempe solos Caini posteros (vtpote quum nondum essent vlli Sethi posteri) coepit: & quidem primum clam & priuatim, atque in animo cususq; (nemo enim repente, vt habet proverbium vetus, fuit turpissimus) tum deinde in communi eorum inter se sermone, ac colloquio de rebus, quas sciebant, possidebantque (eas enim a se, non a Deo esse sentiebat) Denique publicè & manifeste Deum contempserunt, nullo pudore, nulloque vindicta propterea sibi imminentis timore, quum populariter & passim omnes idem sentirent, & facerent. Ex quo tandem publica, & popularis Nominis Dei profanatio secuta est id est, Maiestatis, Potentia, Sapientia, Iustitia, Misericordia, Liberalitatis, ac Beneficentia Dei publica, manifestaq; contemptio, obliuio, imo etiam irrisio, & subsannatio, Gen. 4. 26. Nec ea modo in cateris rebus & hominū actionibus fuit: sed etiā in ipsa Dei inuocatione, & cultu, qui esse inter posteros Caini plane tunc & omnino defitit. Hinc natus Atheismus. Id quod fuit postea publicum homicidium Caini, & scortationem publicam Lamechi tertium teterrimum inter homines primi peccati Adami effectu. Verum illa singulorum peccata erant: haec autem Dominis Dei Profanatio fuit publica, & commune omnium pene hominum, qui tunc in Mundo erant, vitiu, & scelus, Gen. 6 4. Iam vero ex eo, tanquam altissimo pietatis gradu homines deiecti, non modo prolabi: verum metiam ruere in omne nefas, scelus, & flagitiu cœperunt: & quo plures illi ac longaniores fuerunt, eo peiores corruptiorésque deinceps euaserunt. Quid enim sublata ex hominum ore, Dei mentione, & suffocato, deletóque in eorundem conscientiꝫ metu Dei: quid, inquam, inter eos sani, puri, iusti, rečtiꝫ etiam erga alios homines manere potest? Nam vbi Dei veritas & memoria vel prorsus extincta est, vel in mendacium mutata, vel per hominum iniustitia & vim suffocata: In summa, vbi homines notitiam Dei non retinent, natura ipsi suam obliuiscuntur, siúntque ἀσοργοι, superbi, gloriosi, inuentores malorum, oppleti omni iniustitia, scortatione, improbitate, malignitate, Rom. 1.25.26.27.28.29, vti eos postea euasisse quoque constabit ex sequentibus. Atque hoc ipsum fuit velut primus ad Diluuiū illud vniuersale in Mundum accersendum & inducendum riuum & gradus. Contigit autem hæc Profanatio anno Mundi conditi 235. tam paruo tempore tanta ab hominibus post peccatum mala fuerunt inuecta.
units.tr: Therefore, with that perverse race of Cain propagated, and with no great number of the pious yet existing, and the holy stock not yet multiplied, spread abroad and branched out in the world, it followed that there was great strength and reinforcement of vices, and great weakening of virtues among mortals, and at last their destruction followed. And at first the posterity of Cain began to wrong God Himself, whom they did not see with their eyes. Later they wronged their neighbours, among whom they lived and whom they could see. For the impious blaspheme and despise God, whom they regard as invisible and far removed from themselves, more easily than they harm their neighbours whom they see and who are able to defend themselves and are equal to them in strength, and whom they more readily love because of their common nature and fellowship (1 John 4:20; Gal. 5:15). And this contempt of God first arose from the monstrous ambition of men. Since they saw themselves industrious and strong, and abounding in things necessary for this life as well as in pleasures, and since, after the arts were discovered, they sacrilegiously ascribed the praise of all these goods to themselves and their own talent, and not to the true God who was their author, these men readily and willingly sank into this error, and fell so far that they neglected God Himself, and admired only themselves and looked only to themselves. Therefore contempt of God gradually began among such mortals, namely the posterity of Cain alone (since there were as yet no posterity of Seth). At first it was secret and private, and lay in the mind and heart (for no one, as the old proverb says, becomes most shameful all at once), then in their common talk and conversation about the things they knew and possessed (for they felt that these came from themselves and not from God). Finally they openly and publicly despised God, with no shame and no fear of the vengeance hanging over them, since everyone everywhere thought and acted in the same way. From this at last came the public and popular profanation of the name of God, that is, the open and manifest contempt, forgetting, and even mockery and derision of the majesty, power, wisdom, justice, mercy, generosity and beneficence of God (Gen. 4:26). Nor was this only in other matters and human actions, but also in the very invocation and worship of God, which then completely ceased among the posterity of Cain. Hence atheism was born. This was afterwards the public murder by Cain, and the open fornication of Lamech, the third most foul thing among men, as the effect of Adam's first sin. But those were the sins of individuals, whereas this profanation of the name of God was a public vice and crime, common to almost all men who then lived in the world (Gen. 6:4). Now, cast down from this, as from the highest step of piety, men began not only to slip but to rush headlong into every wickedness, crime and disgrace, and the more numerous and long-lived they were, the worse and more corrupt they became. For when the mention of God has been removed from men's mouths, and the fear of God has been smothered and wiped out of their conscience, what soundness, purity, justice, or even uprightness towards other men can remain among them? For where the truth and memory of God have either been wholly extinguished, or turned into a lie, or suppressed by human injustice and violence, in short, where men do not retain the knowledge of God, they forget their own nature, and become ἄσοργοι [without natural affection], proud, boastful, inventors of evils, filled with every injustice, fornication, wickedness and malignity (Rom. 1:25–29), as will also be clear from what follows that they became. This very thing was, as it were, the first stream and step leading to that universal Flood being brought upon the world. And this profanation happened in the 235th year of the world's creation, so quickly after sin did such great evils come into the world among men.

units.la: I- II. Propagatio familiæ Sethi, seu Ec-clesiæ Dei.
units.tr: I-II. The propagation of Seth's family, or the Church of God.

units.la: * MVLTIPLICATVM autem est genus Sethi, atque in eo propagata per summam Dei misericordiam Ecclesia vera, Gen. 5. Nam hæc ipsa per huiusmodi familiarum, & hominum aliorum aliis succedentium continuationes conseruata est, atque etiam per omnes Mundi ætates duravit ante Diluuium vsque ad Noachum: Post Diluuium & Noachum ante Legem datam, vsque ad Abrahami vocationem ex Vr Chaldæorum, quo tempore in vna quadam Mundi, atqꝫ etiā ipsius Sethi familia reiectis aliys fundata, restricta, & coarctata est Ecclesia) Post Abrahami vocationē, vsq; ad Legem populo Israelitico data à Deo in monte Horeb per Mosem, duravit in familia Abrahami. Post Legem datam, vsque ad D. N. Iesum Christum id est Messiam Regem passum pro genere humano in eadem familia, per Iacobum. Post passionem Messiae ex omnibus mundi familijs collecta est, duravitq; ad hec vsque nostra tempora per continuā temporis successionem, & ad hunc vsque annum à Christo nato 1587, quo haec chartis illinebam. Porrò in his Sethi successoribus seu posteris recensendis plures gradus enumerat Moses, quàm in posteris Caini. Hos enim enumerat tantū vsq; ad septimum gradum ab Adamo sic, 1. Cainus ipse pater & autor stirpis & familiae istius. 2. Chanochus.
units.tr: The race of Seth multiplied, and in it the true Church was propagated by God's great mercy, Gen. 5. For it was preserved through successive generations of such families and of other men succeeding one another, and it lasted through all the ages of the world, from before the Flood up to Noah. After the Flood and Noah, before the Law was given, up to the calling of Abraham out of Ur of the Chaldeans, the Church was founded, restricted and confined to one particular part of the world, namely the family of Seth itself, the others having been rejected, and it was reduced to that single line. After Abraham's calling, up to the Law given by God to the Israelite people on Mount Horeb through Moses, it lasted in Abraham's family. After the Law was given, up to our Lord Jesus Christ, that is, the Messiah, King, who suffered for the human race, it lasted in the same family, through Jacob. After the Messiah's suffering it was gathered from all the families of the world, and it has lasted to our own times by a continuous succession through time, and to this year 1587 after Christ's birth, when I was daubing these pages with ink. Moreover, in listing Seth's successors or descendants, Moses names more generations than he does for the descendants of Cain. For he lists them only down to the seventh generation from Adam, as follows: (1) Cain himself, the father and founder of this line and family; (2) Enoch.

units.la: 3. Hiradus. 4. Mechuiael. 5. Methusael. 6. Lemechus. 7. Iabal. Nam Iubal, & Tubal eodem gradu cum Iabale describuntur. Fuerunt enim hi tres filij Lemechi, Gen. 4. Illos autem posteros Sethi ab Adamo (eo non comprehenso) vsque ad nonum gradum, nempe primus est Sethus ipse fons omnium: secundus Enoschus: tertius Cainā: quartus Malaleel: quintus Iared: sextus Henochus: septimus Mathusala: octavus Lemechus: nonus, Noachus Gen. 5. 6, & deinceps. In posteris autem Caini apparet Malorum civitas & successio: in Sethi vero posteris, Bonorum, vti dixi, & Ecclesiæ. Ergo in his quidem Sethi posteris, nepotibus, successoribusq; quos commemorat Moses, nō tamen in omnibus, mansit Ecclesia Dei: ac proinde in eorum familijs solum pijs sonabat & conservabatur praedicatio, memoria, & fides promissionis Dei de venturo Messia, & futuro ex semine Mulieris: vigebant ac retinebantur in ijsdem Sacrificia à Deo fieri in signû illius promissionis iussa: Cultus Dei externus in ijsdem familijs exercebatur qualem describpsimus supra, atq; sibi Deus ipse praescripserat. Idem hi Sethi posteri, sed pij duntaxat, habebant donum Prophetiae, vti apparet ex libro Enochi, Iudae 14. & ex dicto Lemechi, Gen. 5.29, quae est prophetia de futura Dei inexorabilis ira in malos: & Piorum interim conservatione, custodia, & consolatione. Denique in ijsdem illis pijs remanserunt Dei dona spiritualia, velut Fides & sanctitas vitae, Externa morum disciplina, Detestatio impietatis, & Studium propagandi regni Dei: sine quibus omnibus nemo est verè pius nullaq; est vera Dei Ecclesia, 1.Tim. 3.15, Psal. 16.3, Tit. 2.12.13, 2.Tim. 3.16, 1.Pet. 3.20. Illi vero, quos Moses nominat, pij viri fuerunt Dei Ecclesia, Hebr. 11.4.5.6, Iudae epist. verf. 14, 2.Pet. 2.5, Gen. 7.1.
units.tr: 3. Irad. 4. Mehujael. 5. Methushael. 6. Lamech. 7. Jabal. For Jubal and Tubal are listed on the same level as Jabal, since these three were the sons of Lamech, Gen. 4. The descendants of Seth from Adam (not counting Adam himself) up to the ninth generation are these: first, Seth himself, the source of all; second, Enosh; third, Cainan; fourth, Mahalalel; fifth, Jared; sixth, Enoch; seventh, Methuselah; eighth, Lamech; ninth, Noah, Gen. 5, 6, and so on. Among the descendants of Cain, however, there appears a city and succession of evil; among the descendants of Seth, as I have said, there appears a succession of good people and of the Church. So in these descendants, grandchildren and successors of Seth whom Moses records, though not in all of them, the Church of God remained. Accordingly, within their families alone the preaching, memory and faith of God's promise concerning the coming Messiah, to be born from the seed of the Woman, were kept alive and preserved. The sacrifices that God had commanded to be offered as a sign of that promise were still in force and maintained among them, and the external worship of God, of the kind I described above and which God himself had prescribed, was practised in these families. These same descendants of Seth, but only the godly among them, also had the gift of prophecy, as is clear from the book of Enoch, Jude 14, and from Lamech's saying, Gen. 5:29, which is a prophecy of God's future and unrelenting wrath against the wicked, and at the same time of the preservation, protection and comfort of the godly in the meantime. Finally, in these same godly people there remained God's spiritual gifts, such as faith and holiness of life, outward discipline of morals, detestation of impiety, and zeal for propagating the kingdom of God. Without all of these no one is truly godly, and there is no true Church of God, 1 Tim. 3:15, Ps. 16:3, Tit. 2:12-13, 2 Tim. 3:16, 1 Pet. 3:20. Those whom Moses names, however, were godly men who formed the Church of God, Heb. 11:4-6, Jude, verse 14, 2 Pet. 2:5, Gen. 7:1.

units.la: IIII. Translatio visibilis, & miracu- losa Enochi.
units.tr: IIII. The visible and miraculous translation of Enoch.

units.la: SEXTVS ab Adamo, eo non comprehenso, ex posteris Sethi Enochus notorie, visibiliter, & miraculose translatus est à Deo ex hac terra & è conspectu mortalium in cælum sursum, locúmque beatum, vbi ad posteriorem usque resurrectionem omnium (tunc enim, vt ceteri, repraesentabitur) à Deo conseruatur, felix, & vita aeterna fruens, Gen. 5.24, Heb. 11.5, Ecclef. 44.16, Sapient. 4.11. Fuit vero vir ille & pius Gen. 5.22 & & sanctus, probusq; & heres, ac praeco promissionis Dei de futuro Messia: & ventura in mundum, & impios (qui tunc securi in suis sceleribus vivebant) immanis & intolerabilis Dei ira, quae in Diluvio universali poslea apparuit, Gen. 6, 1. Pet. 3. 20, 2. Pet. 2. Has autem praedictiones suas de puniendis postea gravissime hominum illius saeculi immanibus peccatis ad perpetuam rei memoriam ipsorum improborum terrorem, contraque ad piorum consolationem, & fidem scriptis consignauit, ut docet Iudas Apostol. in epist. ver. 14. Porro hac tam mira, & omnibus inopinata Enochi translatio in coelum fuit, estque perpetuum & certissimum testimonium Dei summae cura & benevolentia erga suos, .i. sui timentes homines etiam in media & generali Mundi huius confusione, corruptione, ac intemperie: fuit arrhabo & declaratio felicissimae fortis & conditionis, quae omnibus verè pys post hanc vitam a Deo reseruatur, illisq; destinata est. Hac translatio iam prolabentem, & pene penitus vitijs hominum, licentiaq; peccandi (quae manebat impunita) oppressam pietatem in multis sustentauit, in alijs instauravit, & impios aperte condemnauit, plerosque in Dei metu retinuit. Publica tamen illa nominis Dei profanatio in maiori hominum parte perduravit, imo etiam nihilominus aucta est: fequae audacia ipsa licentiaque scelerate viuendi confirmavit in peius, neque propterea sese copescuit. Ergo ad illud tam mirabile exemplu pauci homines attenderunt, multi illud contempserunt, maior hominum pars irrisit, & vera pietas, quae collabi plurimum coeperat, ruit nihilominus, etiam post translatum Enochum: nec improbi fallì sunt propterea sapientiores, vel meliores, Genef.6.
units.tr: The sixth from Adam, not counting Adam himself, was Enoch, a descendant of Seth. He was notoriously and visibly, and by a miracle, taken up by God from this earth and from the sight of mortals into heaven above, into a blessed place where, until the later resurrection of all (for then he will be restored, as the others will be), he is preserved by God, happy and enjoying eternal life: Gen. 5.24, Heb. 11.5, Ecclus 44.16, Wisd. 4.11. That man was indeed pious, Gen. 5.22, and holy, upright and an heir, and a herald of God's promise concerning the future Messiah, and of the immense and intolerable wrath of God that was to come into the world and upon the impious (who at that time lived secure in their sins), which afterwards appeared in the universal Flood: Gen. 6; 1 Pet. 3.20; 2 Pet. 2. Moreover, he committed these predictions of his, about the most grievous punishments to be inflicted afterwards on the monstrous sins of the men of that age, to writing, for the lasting memory of the thing, as a terror to the wicked themselves and as a consolation and strengthening of faith for the pious, as Jude the Apostle teaches in his epistle, verse 14. Furthermore, this so wonderful translation of Enoch into heaven, unexpected by all, was a perpetual and most certain testimony of God's great care and goodwill towards his own, that is, towards those who fear him, even in the midst of the general confusion, corruption and disorder of this world. It was a pledge and a declaration of the most happy lot and condition which is reserved by God after this life for all who are truly pious, and is destined for them. This translation sustained piety in many who were already slipping and nearly crushed by the vices of men and the licence to sin (which remained unpunished); it restored it in others, openly condemned the impious, and kept most in the fear of God. Yet that public profanation of God's name persisted in the greater part of mankind, indeed it nevertheless grew; and that very audacity and licence of wicked living confirmed them in the worse course and did not on that account restrain them. Therefore few men paid attention to that so remarkable example, many despised it, the greater part of mankind mocked it, and true piety, which had begun to collapse greatly, nevertheless fell, even after Enoch was taken up; nor were the wicked made any wiser or better by it: Gen. 6.

units.la: V. Corruptio Piorum, ac bonorum viro- rum per connubia cum filiabus impio- rum, & improborum hominum.
units.tr: V. The Corruption of the Pious and Good Men through Marriages with the Daughters of the Impious and Wicked Men.

units.la: ALIQVI igitur hac Enochi translatione confirmati remanserát pij, verúmq; Deum ex ipsius verbo colentes, & ad exemplum Enochi coram Deo ambulantes, .i. pie, religiose, sancte, vere, sincere, seq; à mundi illa generali corruptione & nequitia segregantes, qui propterea [Filij Dei] nominantur Gen.6.2. Hi tamen ipsi postea interiecto tempore tum sese ipsos corruperunt, tum ab aliis hominibus sceleratis (cum quibus erant, miscebantur, viuebantque in hoc mundo, ut est 1. Cor.5.10) depravati sunt. Ac depravati quidè, quoniam Corrumpunt bonos mores commercia prava, sicut etiā ipsi Ethnici scribunt, 1.Cor.15.33. Est praeterea magna vis iam recepta sive honestè, sive inhonestè viuendi consuetudinis, quæ, vt ait Augustinus, velut tyrannus, nos, quanuis primum oblectantes tandem tamen ad se traducit, & vincit. Corruperunt vero ipsi quoque pij seipsos per infausta connubia, quæ cum filiabus hominum .i. improborum (quæ filiæ & ipsæ quoque erant improba, lasciuæ, impiè educatæ) illi viri Dei contraxerunt, Gen.6.2. nempe sola earum forma, & corporis venustate delectati, nullā earum impietatis & infidelitatis rationem habentes. Prout igitur illæ mulieres, quantūuis irreligiosæ, viris ipsis & filijs Dei (qui prius tales erant) placebant: sic ab illis in uxores ducebātur. Vnde acciaccidebat, vt & viri ipsi qui antea py religiosique fuerant, corruperentur a suis illis impys vxoribus, vt Salomon rex a suis, 1. Reg. 11. & qui filij ex eo coniugio nascerentur, impie a matribus educarentur, quale esl exemplum Gen. 26. 34. Nehem. 13. 14. Vnde & ipsi liberi quoque euadebat similes matribus suis, nimirum impy, & improbi. Atque sic publica illa, quae iam erat, impietas, improbitasque profana mirifice non tantum sese confirmabat: verum etiam crescebat in dies & augebatur, Gen. 6. 4, & 5.
units.tr: Therefore, some remained pious, strengthened by this translation of Enoch, worshipping the true God from his word and walking before God after the example of Enoch; that is, living piously, religiously, holily, truly and sincerely, and separating themselves from that general corruption and wickedness of the world. For this reason they are called [the sons of God] (Gen. 6:2). Yet these very men afterwards, after some time had passed, were both corrupted themselves and depraved by other wicked men, with whom they were mixed and lived in this world (as in 1 Cor. 5:10). They were depraved indeed, since "evil company corrupts good morals," as the heathen writers themselves also say (1 Cor. 15:33). Moreover, there is great power in a custom once accepted, whether honourable or dishonourable, which, as Augustine says, like a tyrant, though at first it delights us, at last draws us over to itself and conquers us. The pious also corrupted themselves through ill-omened marriages, which those men of God contracted with the daughters of men, that is, of the wicked (daughters who were themselves wanton, impious, and badly brought up) (Gen. 6:2). Namely, delighted by their beauty of form and body alone, they took no account of their impiety and unbelief. So, just as those women, however irreligious, pleased the sons of God themselves (who had been such before), so they were taken by them as wives. Hence it came about that those men who had formerly been pious and religious were corrupted by their impious wives, as King Solomon was by his (1 Kings 11); and the sons born of that union were brought up impiously by their mothers, as the example of Esau shows (Gen. 26:34; Neh. 13:14). Hence also the children themselves turned out like their mothers, namely impious and wicked. And thus that public impiety and profane wickedness, which already existed, was wonderfully not only strengthened but also grew and increased daily (Gen. 6:4, 5).

units.la: VI. Gigantum, & celebrium virorum, qui postea per totum Mundum fue- runt, innotuerunt, Procreatio.
units.tr: VI. The Procreation of the Giants and of the Famous Men Who Afterwards Became Known Throughout the Whole World.

units.la: CAETERVM ex hoc filiorum Dei cum filiabus hominum connubio nati sunt Gigantes: homines illi formidabiles & metuendi, qui tamen postea celebres & memorati fuerunt inter mortales quanis atate Gen. 6. 24. Hi vero omnium huius seculi hominum potentissimi, robustissimique corpore fuerunt, quos alij praeterea perhorrescebat, ac formidabant. Illi igitur cum manifestiores, & immaniores conceptores Dei fuerunt, quam superiores, & Maiores sui, reliquive mortales, qui ea tempestate in Mundo viuebant publice etiam profani: tum vero idem illi erant in ceteros homines iniury, propter immensas corporis vires, quibus reliquos superabant. Itaque suis viribus, suaque inductia (Erant enim & hi quoque inductij viri, & idcirco nomine fama-que celeberrimi pra caeteris) considebant, & caeteros velut se prorsus inferiores per immanem animi superbiam contemnebant. Unde facile prorumpebant ad cateros laedendos, quum essent absq; metu vel publica vindicta (quae tunc nulla de sceleribus a nullo Magistratu sumebatur) vel privata ac talionis, quum aliy ijs propter infirmitatem virium obsistere non valerent. Denig; iam deleto ex eorum, & pene omnium hominum mentibus Dei metu, cultúque: publica inueteratáque iam nominis Dei profanatione recepta: imo omni de Dei potentia memoria prope iam extincta, quid mirū, si praepotentes isti robustique homines, corpore validissimi, animo superbissimi, nullo cuiusquam hominis terrore retenti, Dei etiam contemptores, Gen.6.4, 1.Pet.3.20, 2.Pet.2.5, Math.24.38. & apostata a vera religione (quam a suis patribus didicerant, acceperántque) si, inquam, fuerunt & euaserunt nefandissimi hominum, contumeliosi in alios, ac proinde ceteros (si qui reliqui fortasse erant Dei timentes homines) suo exemplo, audacia, & in ceteros autoritate, prorsus corrumperent, depravarent, audaces ad quodvis scelus facerent? Verum enim semper illud fuit, [Quales Principes, tales & reliquos esse cives, Gen.6.11.12, & 13] Unde ex eo tempore nulla iam publica hominum impietatis & iniustitia, qua etiam iam antea vigebat Gen.6. vincula iniecta sunt, neq; pudore ullo rationeve homines ab ullo maleficio cohibiti fuere. Haec autem contigerunt circa annum Mundi condit pene 908.
units.tr: Next, from this marriage of the sons of God with the daughters of men, the giants were born: formidable and fearsome men, who nevertheless afterwards became famous and renowned among mortals in whatever age. These were indeed the most powerful of all the men of this age, and the most robust in body, whom others moreover dreaded and feared in horror. Therefore, since they were more manifest and more monstrous despisers of God than their superiors and forebears and the other mortals who at that time lived in the world, even openly profane, so they were also at that time wicked toward other men, on account of the immense strength of their bodies by which they surpassed the rest. Accordingly they relied upon their own strength and their own ingenuity (for they were also ingenious men, and on that account most famous above others in name and fame), and in the monstrous pride of their minds they scorned the others as altogether inferior to themselves. Hence they readily broke out to harm the others, since they were free from fear either of public vengeance (for at that time no punishment for crimes was exacted by any magistrate) or of private retaliation in kind, since others could not withstand them on account of the weakness of their strength. Finally, the fear and worship of God having now been wiped out from the minds of them and nearly all men, and public profanation of the name of God having been received and long since ingrained, indeed the memory of God's power having almost wholly died out, what wonder if these mighty and robust men, most strong in body, most proud in spirit, restrained by no terror of any man, were also despisers of God (Gen. 6:4; 1 Pet. 3:20; 2 Pet. 2:5; Matt. 24:38), and apostates from the true religion (which they had learned and received from their fathers); if, I say, they were and became the most accursed of men, insolent toward others, and therefore would they not utterly corrupt and deprave the rest (if any others perhaps were left who feared God), making them bold for every kind of wickedness by their example, their daring, and their authority over the rest? For that has always been true: [Such as the princes are, such also are the other citizens] (Gen. 6:11, 12, 13). Hence from that time no public restraint of human impiety and injustice, which even before had flourished (Gen. 6), was any longer imposed, nor were men restrained from any wrongdoing by any shame or reason. Now these things happened about the year of the world's foundation 908.

units.la: VII. Natiuitas Noachi, & Lemechi patris de eo Prophetia.
units.tr: VII. The birth of Noah, and his father Lamech's prophecy about him.

units.la: IAM vero sic impulso & vrgente Mundo in deploratam plane nequitiam, quum & Dei veneratio in meram illius contemptionem conuersa esset, & quum quoduis audacia & superbia genus in hominibus regnaret: imo etiam in alios homines quanis iniustitia & iniuria exerceri a Gigantibus coepisset, futurum erat, ut postea ne vestigium quidem vllum verae in Deum pietatis, & in proximos charitatis reslaret: nulla vitae sanctitas, nulla pietas amplius, nullaque Dei Ecclesia in mundo superesset: ac proinde solemnis illa Dei Promissio de venturo Messia mundi redemptore periret, nec impleretur: ni Deus, summa sua misericordia, huic tanto, tamque desperato malo mature succurrisset, sapientissime prospexisset, & potentissime obuiam isset. Nam totus Mundus post peccatum primi Hominis non tantum in malo positus erat, (vti nunc quoque est 1. Ioan. 5. 19.) verum in desperatam omnino malitiam ruerat, quae etiam quotidie magis magisque crescebat & invalescebat. Ergo Deus sapientissimus eum hominem nasci voluit, in quo (etiam toto Mundo furiose in omne scelus prolabente) sui tamen metum, verumque cultum retineret: & ex cuius semine Messias ille nasceretur, ac proinde promissionem suam post varias hominum aetates impleret: denique in quo (etiam mortuis sublatisque iis, qui tunc in Mundo reliquerant, pijs) Ecclesiam tamen sua conservaret. Is autem fuit Noachus Lamechi viri pij filius, & ipse quoque valde pius, sanctus, iustus, si quis unquam alius. Gen. 5.28.29, & 6.8.9, Math. 24.38, 1. Pet. 3.20, 2. Pet. 2.5, Heb. 11.7, Eccles. 44.17.18. De quo etiam pater Lamechus manifeste & palam prophetauit, fore, vt illius etate Deus pios consolaretur, & a malitia illa impiorum deplorata eos liberaret. Impios autem prorsus deleret, Gen 5.29. Quod postea in Diluuio vniuersalis sub Noacho cotigit. Natus est autem Noachus anno a condito Mundo 1056, & ante Diluuiu 600. ex patre Lemecho pio, & tunc annum 83. aetate, Gen.5.28.
units.tr: Now when the world had been driven and pressed into utter and desperate wickedness, when the worship of God had turned into plain contempt for him, and when every kind of audacity and pride reigned among men, and when violence and wrong had begun to be inflicted on other men by the Giants, it was bound to happen that afterwards not even a trace of true piety toward God or of charity toward neighbours would remain. There would be no holiness of life, no piety at all, and no Church of God left in the world. The solemn promise of God about the coming Messiah, the Redeemer of the world, would then perish and go unfulfilled, unless God, in his great mercy, had quickly come to the aid of so great and so desperate an evil, had provided for it most wisely, and had met it most powerfully. For after the sin of the first man the whole world was not merely in evil (as it still is, 1 John 5.19), but had fallen into utterly desperate wickedness, which also grew and gained strength every day. So God, in his supreme wisdom, willed that there should be born a man in whom, even while the whole world was headlong plunging into every crime, there would still be preserved the fear of God and the true worship of him; from whose seed the Messiah would be born, and so would fulfil his promise after various ages of men; and in whom, even when those who remained in the world as pious were dead and taken away, he would still preserve his Church. This man was Noah, son of Lamech, a godly man, and himself also very pious, holy, and just, if any man ever was. Gen. 5.28, 29; 6.8, 9; Matt. 24.38; 1 Pet. 3.20; 2 Pet. 2.5; Heb. 11.7; Ecclus 44.17, 18. Concerning him also his father Lamech prophesied clearly and openly that in his time God would be going to comfort the pious, and to free them from that desperate wickedness of the impious; but he would utterly destroy the impious, Gen. 5.29. This happened afterwards under Noah, in the universal Flood. Noah was born in the year of the world 1056, six hundred years before the Flood, to the pious father Lamech, and at that time his father was 83 years old, Gen. 5.28.

units.la: VIII. Corruptissimum vitæ genus & modus, in quo omnis caro corrupe- rat viam suam.
units.tr: VIII. The most corrupt manner and way of life, in which all flesh had corrupted its way.

units.la: CAETERVM & ante natu Noachum (quod fuit annum 600. ante Diluuium, vti diximus: & pluribus adhuc post conditu Mundum) & post eundem editum, crescebat semper, inualescebat, seque in dies magis ac magis dilatabat, amplificabat, & confirmabat inter homines omnes, & in vniuerso hoc Mundo (quàm late incoleretur) hominum impietas in Deum, iniustitia in proximos, audacia superbiaque in ijs ipsis. Nam quum iniquitas & vitiositas a primo primi Hominis Adami peccato sese commouere primum coepisset, in hominum mentibus paulatim & pedetentim postea sese effudit, & crevit: & quidem clam primum & occultè & priuatim in singulorum hominum, qui tunc erant, actionibus tum internis, tum externis (quas tamen non commemorat Moses) semel enim impulsa peccati vis, & concepta in mente hominu, foeda ratio & voluntas ruit semper in peius, & quotidie crescit. Deinde verò etiam palam, manifestè, & publicè sese exeruit, & in apertum imimpudenter eadem nequitia prodyt, primùm in fratricidio a Caino perpetrato Gen.4.8: posteà in violato à Lamecho illo, qui impius fuit, coniugio Gen.4.19: tertio loco in publica & populariter recepta toleratáque Nominis Dei profanatione Gen.4.26: quarto loco, in piorum ipsorum (qui pauci tunc in Mundo reliquerant) per connubia cum filiabus hominum, id est, cum impijs improbisque fœminis deprauatione Gen.6.2: quinto loco, in Gigantum & filiorum ex eo coniugio procreatorum publica superbia, audacia, violentia, & immanitate in Deum ipsum, & reliquos homines: Sexto denique loco, in exemplo & imitatione illius Gigantum immanis vitæ, Gen.6.4. quorum facta reliqui homines secuti & imitati, si quid inter eos reliqui erat vel pudoris hominum ratione, vel verecundia ipsorum peccantium conscientia repressu, vel metus Dei, hoc omne fuit deletum, & prorsus tandem extinctum. His igitur tot machinis tandem expugnata est per longum tempus Dei veritas & notitia, quæ in hominibus posset peccatum superarat. Tot nempe gradibus sese paulatim in altius per annos 1656 subuehens, & conscientia hominum, iustitiaque insitas hominum mentibus à Deo scintillas, sensim cofuetudine peccandi delens & euertens hominum nequitia impunita, publicaque. Ergo tandem illa effecit, & inuexit turpissimum, fœdissimum, corruptissimum vitæ genus inter omnes & singulos mortales, exceptis omnino paucimis, velut una duntaxat, vel altera familia, qualis Lamechi pij, & patriæ Noachi, & ipsiusmet Noachi, & eorum, quos commemorat Moses Gen.5. ex Setho fuisse oriundos. Denique tanta vita hominum impia, iniusta,
units.tr: Moreover, both before Noah was born (which was six hundred years before the Flood, as we have said, and several more years after the creation of the world) and after he was born, the impiety of men toward God, their injustice toward their neighbours, and their audacity and pride toward one another kept growing, gaining strength, spreading and establishing themselves more and more every day among all men, and throughout this whole world (as far as it was inhabited). For when iniquity and vice had first begun to stir from the first sin of the first man, Adam, they gradually and step by step poured out into the minds of men and grew. At first they did so secretly, quietly and privately, in the inward and outward actions of individual men who then existed (which Moses does not record). For once the force of sin had been set in motion and had taken hold in the mind of man, the foul reasoning and will always rush toward the worse and grow daily. Then indeed it also showed itself openly, plainly and publicly, and the same wickedness came out into the light shamelessly: first in the murder of a brother committed by Cain, Gen. 4.8; afterwards in the marriage violated by that Lamech who was impious, Gen. 4.19; third, in the public and popularly accepted and tolerated profanation of the Name of God, Gen. 4.26; fourth, in the corruption of the pious themselves (who were few in the world then remaining) through marriages with the daughters of men, that is, with impious and wicked women, Gen. 6.2; fifth, in the public pride, audacity, violence and savagery of the Giants and of the sons born from that union, against God himself and the rest of men; and sixth and finally, in the example and imitation of that monstrous life of the Giants, Gen. 6.4. Whatever remnant of shame among men, or of modesty by the restraint of the sinners' own conscience, or of fear of God, had remained among them, after the others had followed and imitated their deeds, all this was destroyed and at last utterly extinguished. Thus by these many engines, God's truth and knowledge, which could have overcome sin among men, was at length overthrown over a long time. For over the years, 1656, it lifted itself gradually higher by so many steps, and by the unpunished and public wickedness of men it gradually wiped out and overturned the spark of God implanted in men's minds, the conscience and the sense of justice, through the habit of sinning. Therefore at last it brought about and introduced the most shameful, foul and corrupt way of life among all and each of mortals, with only a very few exceptions, like one or two families only: such as the family of pious Lamech, and of Noah's father, and of Noah himself, and of those whom Moses records in Gen. 5 as descended from Seth. Finally the life of men became so impious, unjust,

units.la: {y} Gen.4.8 etc.: marginal references as printed. & inuerecunda licentia. támque effrenis fuit, vt omnis caro corrumperet viam suam, Gen 6.11.13, id est, vt omnes homines omnem Dei metu abiicerent omnem hominum pudorem amitterent, omne testimonium conscientiae in se delerent: se omni sceleri & flagitio (quantùvis immani, impio horribilis) dederent, quovis modo se homines polluerent, blasphemijs in Deum, cædibus in proximos, adulteriis & scortationibus in mulieres, stupris in mascu los: denique effectum tàdem est, vt essent homines inter se ἀσοργοί, ἀβέλσαι, ἀσπόνδοι, ἀπεσθέες, γονεύσι, θεο-συγεῖς, ἐπεύρεται κακῶν, ἡ πεπληγμένοι πᾶσῃ ἀδικίᾳ, quales vere eos describit Paulus, Rom. 1.29.30 (ad hunc enim Mosis locum plane collimat illic Paulus, & quod Moses breuiter dixit, Paulus ipse fusius explicare voluit) id est, [charitatis expertes, cotumeliosi seu violenti, superbi, parentibus immorigeri, Dei osores, inventores malorum, & plenì omni iniustitia,] & quales quoq; describuntur tum Psal. 58.3.&4: tum etiam Psal.64. Ergo tam improbum, tàmque nefarium vitae genus non primo quoque die & tempore post peccatum Adami in Mundo obtinuit, ac inualuit: sed paulatim emergens, sensim prorepens, pedetentim gliscens, reliquas boni & mali uoluntas hominum animis à Deo relictas suffocans creuit, donec consuetudine peccandi diutina cofirmata neq̄uitia illa hominum sese in apertum tandem proderet, & publice ac impuné grassari auderet: ac denique tandem regnaret. Hoc igitur malum, vt docui, per 235. annos in mente hominis, tanquam in alno matris conceptum est, nempe à peccato hominis, ad Profanationem Nominis Dei. Deinde per annos 821 .i. vsque ad natinatiuitatem Noachi a tempore profanationis nominis Dei editu in lucem & coformatum omnibus suis membris, ac confirmatum est. Denique robustum effectum per annos 600. totos in Mundo regnauit, vsque nimirum ad Diluuium.
units.tr: {y} Gen. 4.8 etc.: marginal references as printed. and shameless licence, and so unbridled, that all flesh corrupted its way, Gen. 6.11, 13; that is, all men cast off all fear of God, lost all shame, and blotted out in themselves all testimony of conscience. They gave themselves over to every crime and disgrace (however monstrous, horrible to the impious), and polluted themselves in every way: with blasphemies against God, murders against their neighbours, adulteries and fornications with women, and debaucheries with males. In the end it came about that men among themselves were unloving [ἀσοργοί], unreasonable [ἀβέλσαι], faithless [ἀσπόνδοι], merciless [ἀπεσθέες], disobedient to parents [γονεῦσι ἀπειθεῖς], hateful to God [θεοστυγεῖς], inventors of evil [ἐφευρεταὶ κακῶν], and filled with all injustice [πεπληγμένοι πάσῃ ἀδικίᾳ], just as Paul truly describes them, Rom. 1.29, 30. (For Paul there aims plainly at this passage of Moses, and what Moses said briefly, Paul himself wished to explain more fully.) That is, [free from charity, insolent or violent, proud, disobedient to parents, haters of God, inventors of evils, and full of all injustice]; and they are likewise described in Ps. 58.3, 4 and also in Ps. 64. So such a wicked and nefarious way of life did not gain strength and prevail in the world on the very first day or at the first time after Adam's sin; but gradually emerging, creeping on by degrees, and growing step by step, it stifled the remaining will to good and evil left in men's minds by God, until that wickedness of men, confirmed by long habit of sinning, at last revealed itself openly and dared to rage publicly and with impunity, and finally to reign. So this evil, as I have shown, was conceived for 235 years in the mind of man, as in the womb of a mother, namely from the sin of man to the profanation of the Name of God. Then, for 821 years, that is, until the birth of Noah, from the time of the profanation of God's Name, it was brought forth into the light and formed and strengthened in all its members. Finally, having become robust, it reigned in the world for six hundred whole years, namely up to the Flood.

units.la: IX. Denuntiatio vniuersalis Diluuij in Mundum futuri, à Deo facta pri- mum Noacho.
units.tr: IX. The universal flood foretold to come upon the world, first made by God to Noah.

units.la: PORRO Deus, qui est iustissimus, ac proinde scelerū vltor grauissimus, quū videret immanem illam hominum malitiam non modo inualuisse, & quotidie crescere: sed plane & immedicabiliter corroborari, ac regnum obtinere, adeo vt omnes omnium hominum non modo externa actiones profana & improba essent: verū etiam interna quoque eorundem cogitationes, cura, & consilia essent & scelerata in Deum, & in Proximum, i. homines iniuria, Gen.6.<, nihilq; aliud homines vel iam apud se meditari, vel priuatim & publice agere quàm nefaria quaque: quum huc, inquam, tam miserū, deploratum, & perditum totius Mundi statum Deus cerneret: homines in deterius semper ruentes animaduerteret, Deum ipsum, vt ita dicam, poenituit, quòd fecisset hominem, illique animalia subiecisset, & ad vsum vita concessisset, eum denique tot donis & beneficijs suis ornasset, Gen.6 6. Itaque quum hanc nequitiam hominum tantam, id est, tam late fusam, tam impunitam, tam popularem, tam publicam in se ipsum hominū impietatem, in aliis homines iniustitiā, in illis ipsis intemperantiam & insolentiam tandiu, id est, pene iam per totos 8 2 1. annos toleraffet Deus, & Mundum, atque aaeo terrâ ipsam (qua homines illos sceleratos ... ) ex tam diuturno cum sceleratis hominibus & impuris contagio videret prorsus pollutam. Gen.6 11, & 12, vbi impuram (Nam propter incolarum peccata terra ipsa, qua ab ipsis habitabatur, Deo exosa est & polluta Psal. 107. 34, Deut. 28) quum, inquam, tam patiens, tamque misericors Deus in homines, & quidem tandiu fuisset: neque illi tamen propterea sanores, sapientiores fieret, neque vllo pacto respiscerent, tadem Deus mundo seu hominibus ipsis, tum eorum ipsorum, tum animalium quoque internecionem comminatus est, eamque suam comminationem Noacho viro pio, iusto, & integro, ipse met, inquit, Deus reuelauit, patefecit, ac praedixit, Gen. 6. 3: nimirum vt eam ipsam hominibus illis impijs denuntiaret Noachus, eoque ad poenitentiam, vitaque emendationem inuitaret, & renocaret. Itaque eadem illa benignitate, qua homines antea ad respiscentiam exspectarat, ita eisdem spatium adhuc & tempus in futurum ad poenitentiam Deus dedit ac concessit, nempe annos totos centum & viginti Gen. 3.3, quos illis praescripsit, si forte postquam suam ruinam, imo internecionem, adeoque etiam omnium rerum & animalium sibi ad vitam conseruandam deperditionem ex Noacho illam praedicante audiuissent, respiscerent, suamque vitam corrigerent, ac in melius mutarent.
units.tr: Moreover God, who is most just and therefore the most severe avenger of crimes, when he saw that that monstrous wickedness of men had not only grown strong and increased daily, but had become thoroughly and incurably entrenched and held sway, so that not only the outward actions of all men were profane and wicked, but also their inward thoughts, cares and counsels were wicked toward God and toward their neighbour, that is, injurious to men (Gen. 6), and that men were now contriving nothing else in themselves, and doing nothing privately or publicly, but what was wicked: when God saw, I say, this so miserable, desperate and ruined state of the whole world, and saw men always rushing headlong into worse things, God himself, so to speak, repented that he had made man, had subjected the animals to him, had granted them for the use of life, and had finally adorned him with so many gifts and benefits (Gen. 6:6). Therefore, since God had endured this wickedness of men, so great, so widely spread, so unpunished, so common, so public an impiety of men against himself, injustice toward one another, and intemperance and insolence in themselves, for so long, that is, for almost the full 821 years, and saw the world, and indeed the earth itself (which those wicked men inhabited...) utterly polluted by such long contagion with wicked and impure men (Gen. 6:11-12), where the earth, polluted, (for on account of the sins of its inhabitants the land itself, which was inhabited by them, was hateful and defiled to God: Ps. 107:34; Deut. 28), when God, I say, had been so patient and so merciful toward men, and indeed for so long, yet they were not on that account made healthier or wiser, nor in any way did they repent, at last God threatened the world, or men themselves, together with their own destruction and also that of the animals, and this threat of his God himself, he says, revealed, disclosed and foretold to Noah, a pious, just and upright man (Gen. 6:3), namely so that Noah might proclaim it to those impious men, and invite and recall them thereby to repentance and amendment of life. Therefore, with the same kindness by which he had previously waited for men to return to their senses, God also gave and granted them space and time for repentance in the future, namely the full 120 years (Gen. 6:3), which he prescribed for them, if perhaps, after hearing from Noah preaching it their ruin, or rather destruction, and thus also the loss of all things and animals kept for the preservation of life, they might repent, correct their lives and change them for the better.

units.la: X. Natiuitas filiorum Noachi.
units.tr: X. The Birth of Noah's Sons.

units.la: INTERIM vero dum publica illa nequitia non tátum inolescit inter mortales, verum etiā impunè, furioseque grassatur: atque etiā postea prædicťum a Deo ad homines perdendos diluuiū,nascuntur tamen Noa-che liberi,quos ex sua vxore suscipit. Tñumero autem tres ante Diluuiū illud uniuersale procreat Noachus, quorum nomina sunt Iaphet,Sem,& Cham, Gen.6.10 Eos verò suscipere & procreare cœpit post annum ætatis suæ quingentesimum, Gen.5 32. Inter hos autem Iaphet fuit natu maximus,& primogenitus, sicut apparet Gen.10:21: Cham minimus natu, vt est Gen.9. 24: Sem ergo fuit secundus,ac medius inter hos tres filios Noachi. Id quod consequens est.Iaphetum enim genuit Noachus anno ætatis suæ quingentesimo exacto: Semum verò anno 502, quemadmodum colligitur ex Genef.11.10. Porrò non solum progeniem aliquam Noacho dare voluit Deus,etiam in media Mundi deprauatione,etiam post denunciatam hominum omnium euersionem,ad eum in tātis malis consolandum:sed etiā tres numero,& quidem masculos eum suscipere voluit, vt maior esset pýs relista spes conseruanda in posterum quoque Ecclesiæ, quum tot liberi in familia illa pia & sanĉta nascerentur. Filiæ verò ante Diluuium non dicitur vllas suscepisse Noachus, quod ad instaurandum post diluuium hunc Mundum,gentesque diffundendas, fuerunt aptiores mares (nam ex masculorū,non ex fœminarum nomine familia vocantur) & quod filij Noachi habuerunt, quisque suam vxorem ex alijs familijs pýs. Ergo Deus Noacho liberos dedit,iam cogitās & decernens & futurum diluuium,& post illud mundum quoque renouandum. In his enim tribus Noachi filijs, & Noacho ipso, eorumque vxoribus conseruatum est semen totius generis humani postea propagādi & spargendi: atque etiam spes noui (qui futurus erat) Mundi hominibus inplendi, quemadmodum postea factum est.
units.tr: Meanwhile, while that public wickedness not only grows among mortals but also rages unpunished and furiously, and although the flood foretold by God to destroy men is still to come, Noah nonetheless has children, whom he begets by his wife. Indeed Noah fathered three sons before that universal flood, whose names are Japheth, Shem and Ham (Gen. 6.10). He began to beget and have them after the five hundredth year of his life (Gen. 5.32). Among these, Japheth was the eldest and firstborn, as appears from Gen. 10.21; Ham was the youngest, as in Gen. 9.24; Shem therefore was the second, and the middle one among Noah's three sons. This follows from the fact that Noah begot Japheth in the five hundredth year of his life, and Shem in the year 502, as is gathered from Gen. 11.10. Furthermore, God wished Noah to have offspring, not only in the midst of the corruption of the world and after the announced overthrow of all men, to console him in such great evils, but also wished him to receive three children, and indeed males, so that a greater hope of preserving the godly remnant for the Church in the future might be kept, since so many children were being born in that pious and holy family. It is said that Noah had no daughters before the flood, because men were more suitable for restoring the world after the flood and spreading the nations (for families are named after the males, not the females); and because Noah's sons each had their own wife from other godly families. Therefore God gave Noah children, already intending and decreeing both the coming flood and the renewal of the world after it. For in these three sons of Noah, and in Noah himself and their wives, the seed of the whole human race was preserved for later propagation and dispersal, and also the hope of filling the new world (which was to come) with men, as was afterwards done.

units.la: XI. Præceptum Dei de fabricanda Ar- ca, in qua pauce reliquie Mundi serua- ntur, factū Noacho, datum à Deo.
units.tr: XI. The command of God, given to Noah, to build the Ark, in which the few remnants of the world are preserved.

units.la: SED quum homines ne quidem post eiusmodi Dei granissimas in se minas à Noacho per plures iam annos denuntiatas emendarentur, Gen. 6.11.12,13, Math. 24.38, Luc. 17.28, Deus decreuit omnino, & quidem breui, quicquid supra terrā superficiem spirabat, delere, & aquis supra terrā immissis penitus perdere, Gen. 7.21.22. Itaque & homines, & animalia omnia, paucissimis tantùm (summâ ipsius misericordiâ) exceptis, quæ Deus ad futuram postea eiusdem rerum generis propagationem, & noua Mundi instaurationem referre voluit. Ac proinde præcepit Deus Noacho, vt Arcam fabricaret, in qua ipse cum vxore, cum filiis suis tribus, & tribus nuribus suis solùm ex hominibus seruaretur in medio terrarum omnium Diluuio, quod statim secutum est, Gen 6.14,18, & 7.13: & in qua eadem Arca ex puris animalibus septena (quæ marem & fœminam in vnoquoque eorum genere septies haberent) ex impuris autem seu immundis animalibus bina tantùm (marem & fœminam bis coplestentia) ad tuendum semen eorum post Diluuium, & genus ipsum propagandum seruabantur, & habebantur Dei iussu, Gen. 7.3.8. 7.3.8.9, &6.19. Sic enim intelligende sunt he voces, [Bina,marem,& fœminam eius] ut bis mas,& bis fœmina in eo genere significentur, nimirum duo paria, seu quatuor in eo genere animalium capita, duo videlicet mares,& duæ fœminæ: Item hæc verba sic sumenda [Septena,marem & fœminâ eius] ut septies mas,& septies in eo genere animalium fœmina sumatur, nimirū terna paria,& prater ea par septimū, quæ continent in summa ex eo animalium genere quatuordecim capita: quod animalia pura & ad sacrificandum Deo,& ad esum hominum necessaria erant. Ergo plura paria ex eo genere servari iubentur, Gen. 8.20,& 9.3. Animalium verò impurorum nullus tunc erat ad sacra & victum usus, neque futurus statim postea erat inter mortales. Ergo eiusmodi vas & Arcam Deus fabricari iussit, in qua pauca omnino illa reliquia mundi iam iam delendi & periturí erant, Dei voluntate, conseruande. Sic autem, atque hæc omnia indicata, prædicta, & præcepta sunt à Deo Noacho, Gen.6.19.20,& 7.2.3.13.14. Sed & formam ipsam, qua fabricanda erat illa Arca, præscripsit quoque eidem Noacho Deus ipse, ut haberet Arca in altitudine 30 cubitos: in longitudine 300: in latitudine 50. Fenestras quoque, quibus à superiore parte clarum lumen hæc eadem Arca reciperet : tectu in cubiti altitudinem assurgens: demum ostiu in latere. Ipsam verò Arcam seu eius internum spatium in tria tabulata, seu mansiones tres distingui,& distribui Deus voluit, Gen.6.14.15. Ipsam denique totam introrsum & extrorsū sedulo pice obduci & picari iussit,& omne ciborum (quibus homines & animalia ingressura vescerentur) genus collẽctiũ in eadem Arcam inferri a Noacho importari, coaceruãriq;, Deus precipit, Gen. 6. 21 quod satis esset ad omnium in eam intrantium victum.
units.tr: BUT since men were not reformed even after such most grave threats of God, announced to them by Noah for many years (Gen. 6.11-13; Matt. 24.38; Luke 17.28), God decided altogether, and that soon, to destroy whatever breathed upon the surface of the earth, and to utterly destroy it by waters poured over the earth (Gen. 7.21-22). And so men and all animals, with only a very few excepted (by his own great mercy), whom God wished to keep for the future propagation of the same kinds of things and the new restoration of the world. Accordingly God commanded Noah to make an ark, in which he himself with his wife, his three sons and their three wives alone would be preserved from among men, in the midst of the universal flood that immediately followed (Gen. 6.14-18; 7.13); and in which same ark, of clean animals seven pairs (that is, seven males and females of each kind) and of unclean or impure animals only two (a male and its female, the two of each kind) were kept and held by God's command, to protect their seed after the flood and to propagate the kind itself (Gen. 7.3, 8-9; 6.19). For these words must be understood thus: [two, male and its female] so that the male and female are signified twice in that kind, namely two pairs, or four individuals of that kind of animal, two males and two females; likewise the words [seven, male and its female] are to be taken so that the male is taken seven times and the female seven times of that kind of animal, namely three pairs and besides them a seventh pair, which in total contain fourteen individuals of that kind of animal: because the clean animals were necessary both for sacrificing to God and for the food of men. Therefore more pairs of that kind are ordered to be kept (Gen. 8.20; 9.3). Of the unclean animals there was then no use for sacrifice or food, nor would there be any afterwards among mortals. Therefore God ordered such a vessel and ark to be built, in which by God's will those few remnants of a world now about to be destroyed and perish were to be preserved. And thus all these things were indicated, foretold and commanded by God to Noah (Gen. 6.19-20; 7.2-3, 13-14). But God himself also prescribed to the same Noah the very form in which that ark was to be built: that the ark should have a height of 30 cubits, a length of 300, and a breadth of 50. Also windows, through which clear light would enter the ark from above, the roof rising to a height of one cubit; finally a door in the side. God wished the interior space of the ark to be divided and distributed into three decks, or three storeys (Gen. 6.14-15). Finally he ordered it to be carefully coated with pitch inside and outside, and God commands that every kind of food, gathered together, be brought into and stored in the same ark by Noah, which would suffice for the sustenance of all who entered it (Gen. 6.21).

units.la: XII. Diluuium vniuersale in terris a Deo immissum.
units.tr: XII. The universal flood sent by God upon the earth.

units.la: QVARE rebus omnibus sic comodè ad sua primum quidem Ecclesiæ conseruationem, postea vero ad Mundi huius instaurationem, denique hominum atque animaliū propagationem præceptis, & a Noacho præparatis, effectisque, Diluuium a Deo in vniuersa terra faciem immissum est, Gen. 7. 1. Nec enim homines respuerant quauis & per integros 120 annos minas Dei de eo futuro certissimas ex Noacho audyssent, & ipsa Arcam iam paratam oculis suis cernerent. Manebant igitur prorsus surdi cæcique ad hæc omnia spectacula, & impœnitentes omnino homines, licet comoniti, excitati, expectatique a Deo diutissime fuissent. Imo vero quatumuis tempus a Deo destignatum illis ad pœnitentiam, & a Noacho ysdem definitum appropinquaret, instaretque proximè, tamen securi, vt prius, & quasi remoti procul a Dei iudicio suis ceruicibus iam iam tamen imminenti, ludebat, ridebant, coniuabantur, epulabātur, nubebant fœminæ, viri vxores ducebant, Deum omnes spernebant, vt antea. Math. 24. 28, Luc 17. 28, Gen. 6 13: & alij in alios iniuriij erant, 2. Pet. 2. 3. Ergo anno 601. ætatis Noachi, Gen. 7. 6, mense eius anni secundo, die decimo eiusdem mensis, nempe diebus septem antequam catarractli cœli rumperentur, imbresque & pluuiæ illæ horribiles (quæ totam terram summerserūt, operueruntque) è cœlo deciderent. Deus iussit Noachum cum uxore, tribus filijs, & nuribus suis ingredi in Arcā Gen.7.4. Primus igitur Noachus & filij eius ⁊. Homines primi in Arcam intrarunt, Gen.7.4.7.8, ut illi animalia in Arcam proximè (Deo sic impellente) ingressura exciperent, & in suos nidos, suásque cellulas & mansiones sigillatim & cōmodè, pro cuiusque Animalis natura & specie, distribuerent, ac collocaret. Ergo postquàm homines illi (nimirum ottō duntaxat Animæ, 1. Pet.3.20) in Arcam fuerunt Dei iussu ingressi Gen.7.1.2: intra septem dies sequentes omnia tum munda, tum immunda animalia, quæ Deus in Arca seruari voluit, postea sunt (eodem Deo arcano motu illa cieté) ingressa in Arcam ad Noachum vltrò & sponte, posita sæua, feroci, & crudeli (quæ in quibusdam feris est) natura sua, vt capi, tractari, & pasci commodè & tutò possent à Noacho in Arca, & à filys eius per totum, quo cum ys futuri erant, tēporis, ⁊. anni spatium. Porrò exceptis ys tum hominibus, tum animalibus, quæ in Arca tempore Diluuij fuerunt, reliqua omnia viuentia & spirantia, quæ tunc erant in vniuersa terra superficie, perierunt, velut Iumenta, fera bestiæ, Reptilia, Volatilia, Gen.7.22. Pisces igitur eo numero non comprehenduntur, etsi eorum plerosq; tunc mortuos fuisse ob vim illam nimiā aquarum non est incredibile. Reliqua verò viuentia omnia ab aquis suffocata sunt. Illa enim etiam montiū, licet altissimorum, cacumina totis quindecim cubitis superarunt, Gen.7.20. Pluit verò per quadraginta dies continuos effusissimè & copiosissimè é cœlo: Deinde mare ipsum per se intumuit: Catarractæ cœli sese ruperunt: fontes abyssi sese aperuerunt. Unde tandem fuit infinita & immensa vis aquarum, quæ totam terræ faciem altissimè operuerunt, Gen. 7. 11. 17. 18. 19. Atqui sic Diluuium vniuersale fuit, quod viuentia omnia extinxit.
units.tr: Since all things had been so conveniently prepared, first by the precepts of God and the work of Noah for the preservation of the Church, then for the restoration of this world, and finally for the propagation of humankind and the animals, God sent the flood upon the whole face of the earth (Gen. 7.1). For the people had not rejected Noah's warnings, and for a full 120 years they had heard from him the most certain threats of God concerning the coming judgment, and they could see the ark already built before their eyes. They therefore remained utterly deaf and blind to all these spectacles, and they were wholly unrepentant, although they had been admonished, roused, and waited upon by God for a very long time. Indeed, even though the time appointed by God for their repentance, and fixed by Noah, drew near and was close at hand, they remained secure as before, as if far removed from God's judgment, which was already hanging over their necks. They mocked, they laughed, they feasted and banqueted, women married and men took wives, and all of them despised God as before (Matt. 24.38; Luke 17.28; Gen. 6.13), and they wronged one another (2 Pet. 2.3). Therefore, in the six hundredth and first year of Noah's life (Gen. 7.6), in the second month of that year, on the tenth day of the same month, that is, seven days before the floodgates of heaven were burst open, those dreadful showers and rains, which submerged and covered the whole earth, fell from heaven. God commanded Noah to enter the ark with his wife, his three sons, and their wives (Gen. 7.4). So Noah and his sons went in first; the first men entered the ark (Gen. 7.4, 7, 8), so that they might receive the animals that were about to enter the ark immediately afterward (God thus driving them on), and might distribute and place them individually and conveniently in their nests, cells, and quarters, according to the nature and kind of each animal. Therefore, after those men (namely, only eight souls, 1 Pet. 3.20) had entered the ark at God's command (Gen. 7.1, 2), within the following seven days all the animals, both clean and unclean, which God willed to be preserved in the ark, afterward entered the ark of their own accord and freely to Noah, roused by that same hidden motion of God. Their fierce, savage, and cruel nature, which some wild beasts have, was laid aside, so that they could be handled, tended, and fed conveniently and safely by Noah in the ark and by his sons throughout the whole period of time, a year and some days, that they were to be together. Moreover, apart from those men and animals who were in the ark during the time of the flood, all the other living and breathing creatures that were then on the surface of the whole earth perished, such as the beasts of burden, the wild beasts, the reptiles, and the birds (Gen. 7.22). Fish are therefore not included in that number, although it is not incredible that most of them died at that time because of the great force of the waters. But all the other living things were suffocated by the waters. For the waters rose fifteen cubits above even the tops of the mountains, however high they were (Gen. 7.20). It rained copiously and profusely from heaven for forty continuous days; then the sea itself swelled up by its own force, the floodgates of heaven burst open, and the fountains of the deep broke forth (Gen. 7.11, 17, 18, 19). Thus at last there was an infinite and immense force of waters, which covered the whole face of the earth to the highest point. And so there was a universal flood, which destroyed all living things.

units.la: CAPUT II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: Disputata, & agitata quædam in his duodecim Historiæ capitibus.
units.tr: Some matters disputed and discussed in these twelve chapters of the History.

units.la: NTESTARI primùm omnium libet nos pleráque in quæstionem non vocaturos in hac sectione & Epoche tertia, quæ perplures tamen tùm Græci, tùm Latini Patres, & Ecclesiastici scriptores velut dubia proponunt, vexántque, propterea quòd illa vel ex falso annorû numero, vel ex non obseruato rerum gestarum ordine promanant, quum suum potius in eis iudicium, quàm Mosis historiam secuti fuerint Patres illi, & annorum numerum ex versione 70, non ex ipso Mose sumpserint, ac supputarint. Itaque hic & Philo, quanuis Iudæus, in Biblis. Antiquitat. multa perturbata habet: & Augustinus quoque lib. 15. Ciuit. Dei: sed & Zonaras etiá Tomo 1. Animalium, vt alios omittam. Nos autem & seriem temporis, & annorû supputationem, quam Moses sés, id est, ipsa veritas habet, sequimur. Itaque plerasque eiusmodi quæstionum euitamus.
units.tr: I wish first of all to state that in this section and in the third epoch we shall not call into question most of the things which many Greek and Latin Fathers and ecclesiastical writers put forward as doubtful and dispute, because these difficulties arise either from a false count of years or from a failure to observe the order of events. Those Fathers preferred their own judgment to the history of Moses, and took their count of years from the Septuagint rather than from Moses himself, and calculated from it. So Philo, though a Jew, has many confusions in his Antiquities of the Bible, and Augustine too in book 15 of The City of God, and Zonaras also in the first volume of his Annals, to omit others. We, however, follow the sequence of time and the reckoning of years that Moses gives (sés, that is, the truth itself). So we avoid most questions of this kind.

units.la: Ad I. Natiuitas Enoschi.
units.tr: I. The Birth of Enosch.

units.la: Primum igitur de Enoschi natiuitate agamus, in qua quaritur Quid nomen [Enosch] Hebraicè, Græcè vero, sicut describsit Lucas 3. 38, ἐνὼς, significet, vtque à voce [Adam] differat. R. Augustin. lib. 15. Ciuit. Dei, cap. 17. de hac duplici quastione sic ait, [Enos filius Sethi interpretatur homo, non sicut Adā: Et ipsum enim nomen interpretatur Homo, sed commune perhibetur esse in illa linga (id est, Hebræa) Masculo, & fœmine. Vnde non ambigitur sic appellatam fuisse fœminam Enam proprio nomine, vt tamen Adam (quod interpretatur Homo) nomen esset amborum. Enos autem sic interpretatur Homo, vt hoc non posse fœminā nuncupari periti linguæ illius asseuerent, tāquam filius resurrectionis (Seth enim est resurrectio) vbi non nubāt, neq; vxores ducant. Quare & hoc non in cassum notandum arbitror, quòd in his generationibus, quæ propagantur ex illo qui appellatur Seth, quiū genuisse dicatur filios, filiasque, nulla ibi genita fœmina nominatim expressa est. In his autem, quæ propagantur ex Cain, in ipso fine, quoniamque protenduntur, nouissima fœmina genita nominatur, vt intelligatur Ciuitatem terrenam, cuius conditor fuit Cain, & initium & finem habere terrenum.] Illius enim radix nimirum Eua nominatur. Terrenam autem Ciuitatem, (quæ in Seth designatur) nec generare, nec generari carnaliter. Nec enim ibi erit carnalis generatio, quum nos illuc perduxerit regeneratio. Hæc Augustinus, qua certè quidem sunt subtiliora, & omnino haud vera. Nam fœminæ siue uxores ab Hebræis vocantur quoque [Nasschim] quasi [Enasschim] ab eodem themate. à quo & vox [Enosch] Ex quo fit, vt illa Augustini obseruatio sit parum firma, & solida. Melius igitur vir prientissimus, & literarum Hebraicarum callentissimus, earundemq; regius olim Lutetiæ Parisiorum Professor Ioannes Mercerus sic docuit, Nomen [Adam] ad eius ex humo formationem respicere: At [Enosch] ad conditionem infirmam, imbecillam, arumnosam, & laboris periculiq; plenam, in quâ Homo postea per peccatum incidit, ac prolapsus est. Vnde summa infirmitatis significatio in ea voce inest, quæ infirmitas tam ad masculos, quam fœminas, imò ad gentes omnes sexum, & conditionem hominum pertinet, vt est in Psal 9.12: [Sciant gentes, inquit Dauid, quod Enosch id est homo sunt.] Et hæc sunt verissima. Nonnulli vocabulum Enosch dici putant, quòd cito homines in oblivionem adducantur. Sic Eusebius lib. II. Præparat. Euangel. cap. 4. quanquam idem eiusdem operis lib. 7. cap. 3. vult [Enos,] (qui idem est & Enosch) significare id, quod vox [Homo] id est mortalem, & infirmam conditionem. Alij verò Enosch deriuari putant ab ea radice Hebræa, quæ Desperare declarat. Vnde Enosch illis est desperatus, & violentus. Sic Philo lib. de Nomin. Hebraic. in Genesi. Verùm ista nutant. Ex quo apparet quanta fuerit Caini & Sethi in primogenito quisque suo nominando differentia. Nam Cainus hypocrita & malus etiam postquam à Dei facie pulsus fuerat, & ex Dei Ecclesia eiectus, filium tamen suum priprimogenitum appellauit [Hanoch,] id est eruditum, bene initiatum & morigeratum. At vero Sethus vir pius & bonus vocauit primogenitū suum [Enosch] .i. mortalem & erumnosum. Sic fere hypocritae speciosa omnia spectant & sequuntur, ut videantur ab hominibus veri fideles res ipsae ex veritate æstimāt ut Deo seruiant. Q. Utrum fuerit Enosch primogenitus Sethi, quum demum anno illius 105 natus dicatur: alij vero, Sethiq; posteri maturius liberos suscepērint, velut Enosch ipse anno ætatis suæ 90. Kenan: Kenan autem Malalahalaelem anno 70: Malalahalael anno 65.
units.tr: First, then, let us treat of the birth of Enosch. Here the question is what the name [Enosch] means in Hebrew, and what Greek [ἐνὼς] means, as Luke writes it in 3:38, and how it differs from the word [Adam]. Augustine, in book 15 of The City of God, chapter 17, speaks thus on this double question: "Enos, son of Seth, is interpreted as 'man,' but not in the same way as Adam. For the name Adam is itself interpreted as 'man,' but in that language (that is, Hebrew) it is held to be common to male and female. Hence there is no doubt that the woman was called Enam by a proper name, yet Adam, which means 'man,' was the name of both.
